text:
jane_orbit: Hi team — we accepted an AWS Accelerator grant (StartAI program) yesterday but the credits aren't showing in our Redwood balance. AWS invoice shows the grant was issued. Can you check?
sophia_support: sorry about that, @jane_orbit. Can you paste the AWS account ID (12 digits) and the marketplace order id/entitlement id you see in AWS?
jane_orbit: account 123456789012, entitlement arn:aws:marketplace:us-east-1::subscription/entitlement/ent-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
sophia_support: got it. I'm going to pull the entitlement events. @mike_billing fyi — customer reports grant visible in AWS but not applied to Redwood account.
mike_billing: thanks @sophia_support. Usually this is either a webhook delivery gap or a tenant mapping mismatch (payer vs linked account). I'll check the delivery logs.
marketplace-bot: webhook delivered — 200 OK — payload id 8f7c3a2b (received 2026-03-10T16:02:12Z)
eng_platform_tom: quick check — do we have the external_id / tenant tag from the customer's AWS account? If the entitlement lands against the payer but their Redwood account is mapped to a linked subaccount it'll not auto-apply.
sophia_support: @jane_orbit can you confirm whether 123456789012 is the payer account or a linked member?
jane_orbit: that's the linked member (we use a consolidated billing setup). The payer is 210987654321.
eng_platform_tom: that explains it. The webhook came through but the entitlement was associated to the payer id (210987654321) in our system; your Redwood tenant is mapped to the linked account 123456789012 so the match failed.
sophia_support: sorry about the mismap — we'll re-associate. @mike_billing can you run the manual entitlement requeue for ent-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h to the linked account?
mike_billing: running requeue now via admin endpoint. curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/entitlements/reprocess" -d '{"entitlement_id":"ent-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h","target_aws_account":"123456789012"}' --auth @svc-billing-key
marketplace-bot: reprocess job queued — job id reproc-9921
mike_billing: logs: 
```
[INFO] fetched entitlement ent-0a1b2c4
[INFO] matched marketplace payload -> payer 210987654321
[WARN] tenant mapping not found for linked account 123456789012, applying mapping override
[INFO] applied credit: customer_id=orbit-42 amount_usd=5000 token_credit=500000
[INFO] ledger updated, posting balance change
```

sophia_support: I see the ledger change. @jane_orbit you should see credits in your console in a minute. Can you confirm?
jane_orbit: checking... I can see the promo balance now, +$5,000. Thank you!! :tada:
sophia_support: great. Sorry for the confusion — looks like our auto-matching needs to better handle payer/linked cases. @eng_platform_tom can we add a fallback that checks linked->payer relationships when a direct account match fails?
eng_platform_tom: yes, filing an action item: INF-4271 — fallback to check Organization/ConsolidatedBilling relationships during entitlement match. I'll add a short-term mitigation to log more detail and attempt auto-association for confirmed linked accounts.
mike_billing: I'll also add a dashboard alert for entitlements that land on payer accounts that have >1 linked member in our mapping table.
sophia_support: marking this thread resolved for now. @jane_orbit if anything else pops up DM me and we'll reopen.
jane_orbit: appreciate it, @sophia_support and team. Fast follow — is there a public doc about how to map payer vs linked accounts for marketplace grants?
sophia_support: not yet, I'll draft a short KB and post in #support-resources — will ping you when done.
eng_platform_tom: note for the KB: include sample curl to reprocess and a note about providing both payer and linked AWS account ids.
sophia_support: closing out. :white_check_mark:
